question: What makes it possible for a robot to build?

answer.answer:
Building robotically rests on six cited requirements, of which only one is a machine: a robotic arm (RE2), plus path-planning (PR12), a highly standardised (AT7) component set, prefabrication/off-site work (PR2), a workable delivery/business model/work culture (RI12) and a mobile factory (CO12). The two sharpest facts are negative: the mobile factory is a direct cited precondition of robotic assembly carried by none of the 50 coded cases, and the path-planning link by only 2, even though 26 cases draw on path-planning and 13 on robotic assembly in their own right. Against that, significant human involvement (RE6) is drawn on by all 50 cases, so what makes a robot build is, in the record, still largely people, standardisation and a factory-like way of organising work rather than the arm itself. The record has no term "robot" as such; the nearest anchor is robotic assembly (PR4), which is what this answer is built on.

**What the cited literature says is required**

PR4 "Robotic assembly" (Process) is the anchor. It carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, all of them listed in the context, and 13 of the 50 coded cases draw on it. [1] Its upstream requirements, read by relation rather than by arrow direction, are:

- RE2 "Robotic arm" (Resource), which enables robotic assembly (DEP11, carried by 12 of the 50) [1] and which robotic assembly in turn depends on (DEP24, also carried by 12) [1]. 22 of the 50 cases draw on RE2. [1] Backed by peer-reviewed evidence.
- AT7 "Highly standardised" (Attribute), which enables robotic assembly (DEP88, carried by 10 of the 50), on the grounds that Japanese automated erection systems rely on standardised prefabricated components [1]. 25 of the 50 cases draw on AT7. [1]
- PR12 "Path-planning" (Process), a precondition for robotic assembly (DEP23), carried by only 2 of the 50 [1], while 26 of the 50 cases draw on PR12 [1].
- PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site" (Process), a precondition of robotic assembly (DEP55, carried by 4 of the 50): automated overhead delivery and assembly requires extensive prefabrication and unification of materials [1]. 20 of the 50 cases draw on PR2. [1]
- RI12 "Delivery/business model/work culture" (Risk), which robotic assembly depends on (DEP61, carried by 2 of the 50), because robotics adoption in precast production rests on the environmental and organisational context [1]. 16 of the 50 cases draw on RI12. [1]
- CO12 "Mobile factory" (Condition), which enables robotic assembly (DEP42) on the argument that all-weather cover allows welding and assembly to proceed in a normal manner even in rain, and which is carried by 0 of the 50 coded cases [1]. Only 1 of the 50 cases draws on CO12 at all. [1] This is the same relation as RE2, AT7 and PR12 hold, a direct precondition, and the literature asserts it while none of the 50 exhibits it.

These six differ by an order of magnitude in how widely they are drawn on: AT7 at 25 and PR12 at 26 against CO12 at 1. Of PR4's own cited requirements, RE2's edge is carried by 12 of the 50 and CO12's by none.

**One step further back**

Path-planning itself has requirements the context lists: RE4 "3D scanner/sensor/camera/ICT" is a precondition of path-planning (DEP39, carried by 22 of the 50), since localisation via onboard sensors is a fundamental prerequisite for autonomous operation [1]; path-planning also depends on CO16 "3D point-cloud" (DEP30, carried by 9 of the 50) [1]; and RI5 "Location dependent/site constraint" constrains it (DEP44, carried by 15 of the 50), because reliable GNSS signals are typically unavailable indoors [1]. RE8 "Machine Learning/AI algorithm" and [1] RE1 "Parametric/computational/data-driven algorithm/machine code" each enable path-planning (DEP3 carried by 5, DEP7 by 7) [1].

**What the record adds that no edge shows**

RE6 "Significant human involvement" is drawn on by 50 of the 50 coded cases and carries no cited dependency edge at all [1], so the literature has not connected it, yet it is the most consistently present element in the whole coded record. Similarly, 44 of the 50 cases draw on AR9 "Automated production workflow" (Artefact) [1], and that workflow depends on RI6 "Require workforce training" (DEP100, carried by 38 of the 50), since high sophistication of digital technologies prohibits adoption by less technologically familiar workers [1]. 44 of the 50 cases draw on RI6. [1] Training and human presence are, on the numbers, more universal than any hardware.

**Deployed processes**

The context carries four deployed records that actually perform assembly-type work, though it does not link them to particular enablers. census_RXH3-2 performs assembly, steelwork and welding on the structural core, the building envelope, the facade or curtain wall, at technology readiness level 9 [2], and was developed by Firm_143, working in steel. census_RXH4-1 was adopted to address cost and labor and performs assembly and concrete work on the structural core, envelope, facade or curtain wall, at technology readiness level 9 [3], with Firm_166 as manufacturer. census_RXM11-4, adopted to address cost, labor and integration, performs 3D printing, assembly, concrete work and shotcrete, at technology readiness level 8 [4], manufactured by Firm_077 and Firm_151. census_RXM11-6 performs 3D printing, concrete work, shotcrete and surface treatment and sits at technology readiness level 7 [5], with Firm_020 and Firm_151. That the mature deployments here are concrete and steel assembly at high readiness is consistent with the standardisation and prefabrication preconditions above, but the context does not record which enablers these cases draw on, so that remains an alignment rather than an established link.

**What it brings, and what to watch**

Robotic assembly amplifies VA2 "Reduce time/improve productivity/efficiency" (DEP95, carried by 13 of the 50) [1], amplifies VA6 "Reduce cost" (DEP54, carried by 7 of the 50) [1], and enables VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints" (DEP21, carried by just 1 of the 50) [1]. The quality-control claim is therefore the weakest of the three in the deployed record. On the risk side, beyond training, 14 of the 50 cases draw on RI1 "Increase uncertainty in production" [1] and 13 draw on RI20 "Work safety concern" [1]; the one route to safety visible here is CO6 "Human-robot interaction" mitigating RI20 (DEP57, standards evidence, carried by 4 of the 50) [1], and RI20 carries three cited edges in total, so the others are simply not in front of me.
